newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares sink as European markets darken mood.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares sink as European markets darken mood.

text.p: Dutch shares ended slightly lower on Wednesday, as red screens of surrounding stock markets spoiled an early morning surge.
The AEX index of main shares closed 1.18 points lower at 804.95, after reaching an intraday high of 815.18.
The midcap AMX index ended up 8.33 points at 1289.53.
"With both France and Germany losing ground, our strength is also fading," one dealer said.
Dealers said market sentiment was severely hit by rumours of privately commissioned polls showing the left wing in a strong position for France's elections on Sunday.
"People are getting quite scared over what's happening in France," another dealer said, adding increasing worries were likely to give the Dutch share market a low profile this week.
"If the Socialist Party wins, it'll be a drama," he said.
Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis released a higher than expected first quarter net profit of 204 million ECUs ($233.4 million), up 30 percent from the year-ago period.
Analysts were positive over the forecast of a 10 to 15 percent lift in full year earnings, but the share closed only 0.80 guilders higher at 82.30 guilders.
"That was just good news falling in a bad market," one dealer said.
The high-tech sector as a whole performed well, with Baan ending 1.20 higher at 118.20 guilders, as a bullish newspaper article lured investors into the stock.
Shares in ASM Lithography closed up 50 cents at 103.50 guilders after market rumours of bid interest from Hitachi or Intel of the U.S. had pushed the stock to an intraday high of 108.30 guilders.
Both Hitachi and ASML denied there were any bid talks underway.
"All these rumours nowadays seem to be generated on the floor of the stock exchange itself. It goes with the excitement that prevails in the sector," SNS Securities analyst Bert Siebrand said.
Philips, which owns 23.90 percent of ASM Lithography closed down 0.30 guilders at 108.00.
Packaging group Van Leer added 2.10 or over five percent to 43.00 as German sector peer Schmalbach-Lubeca unveiled a growth strategy and said it might hike dividends.
"That news must have spilled over onto our market as well," one dealer said.
Temporary employment agency Randstad added 3.00 guilders to close at 194.50.
One dealer said the issue of Falcons -- Fixed term Agreements for Long-term Call Options on Netherlands' securities -- on some three percent of the shares might be behind the rise.
Shares in retail and business services group Vendex closed 0.70 higher at 109.90.
"With the subscription to Vedior mega-overwritten, one turns to Vendex to get some Vedior shares later on," one dealer said.
Shares in Vedior, the temp and services offshoot from Vendex, are to be listed on the stock exchange on June 5.
